passage:
Civics teacher's note, Class 10, Friday.
After the assembly where a visiting youth leader spoke, Jaya came to my desk glowing and repeated whole lines of his speech. Her friend Gautam rolled his eyes and said it was only words. I did not correct either of them.
I asked Jaya, "What did he say he has actually done?" She was quiet, then said she didn't know. We looked up the group's public reports together. She wrote three questions in her notebook: what they have built, who pays for it, and what is not in the speech.
She told me the speech still gave her goosebumps, and I said she is allowed that. I will check in on Monday.

qa.q: What three questions did Jaya write in her notebook?
qa.a: She wrote what they have built, who pays for it, and what is not in the speech.

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling after the speech, and how do you know?
qa.a: She felt thrilled: she came to the desk glowing, repeated whole lines, and later said the speech still gave her goosebumps.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped Jaya think for herself?
qa.a: The teacher asked what the leader had actually done and looked up the public reports with her, without lecturing, so Jaya wrote her own questions.

qa.q: Why might Gautam have rolled his eyes?
qa.a: Gautam may be wary of big speeches and think they are only words, though the eye roll alone doesn't show what he really thinks.

grounding: Shows a teen thrilled by a leader's speech and guided to ask what he does, who benefits and what is hidden.

passage:
The rally ground was packed, the loudspeakers crackling, and it had started to drizzle. Madhuri, pressed between strangers, couldn't hear her friend Kavitha half the time. But she heard the leader.

He spoke about young people building a new city, about dignity, about jobs for everyone. The crowd roared. Madhuri felt goosebumps down her arms. She was shouting along before she knew it.

On the crowded bus home, soaked, she was still glowing. "Wasn't he amazing?"

Kavitha, wringing out her dupatta, said, "He was. What has he actually done, though? He's been in the council for five years."

Madhuri didn't know.

That night, with the power flickering, they looked up his council record on Kavitha's phone. Two promised flyovers, one finished. A school road still broken. A contract for his brother-in-law's firm.

Madhuri was quiet. "The speech was still good."

"It was," Kavitha said. "Now we know what to ask him next time."

qa.q: How long has the leader been in the council, according to Kavitha?
qa.a: He has been in the council for five years.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling during the speech?
qa.a: Madhuri felt thrilled and swept up, with goosebumps, shouting along with the crowd.

qa.q: What did Madhuri and Kavitha do that was wise after the rally?
qa.a: They looked up his council record to see what he had actually done and who had benefited, instead of relying only on the speech.

qa.q: How does Kavitha see the leader?
qa.a: Kavitha thinks he speaks well, but wants to judge him by his record, not only by how the speech feels.

grounding: It shows a teen thrilled by a charismatic leader's speech who enjoys the inspiration, then asks what the leader actually does and who benefits.

passage:
The young councillor who spoke at the school's annual day was the best speaker Ojas had ever heard. She talked about clean parks, safe streets, libraries for every ward. The whole auditorium stood up and clapped. Ojas's heart was racing.

At home in their Jayanagar flat, he told his cousin Vijay, "I want to work for her when I'm older."

Vijay, who was in college, didn't laugh. "Okay. What has she done so far?"

"She said she'd build libraries."

"Did she?"

Ojas didn't know. So they checked the ward website together. One library had been opened, in fact. Two parks had been cleaned. But the "safe streets" plan was only on paper, and the contract for the park lights had gone to a firm that had also donated to her campaign.

Ojas frowned. "So is she good or bad?"

"Maybe both. That's what you check," Vijay said. "Enjoy the speech. Then read the record."

Ojas wrote her name in his notebook, with three questions under it.

qa.a: She spoke at the school's annual day.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling after the speech?
qa.a: Ojas felt inspired and excited, his heart racing, and wanted to work for her one day.

qa.q: What did Vijay teach Ojas to do after being inspired?
qa.a: Vijay taught Ojas to check what the leader has actually done and who benefits, using the ward website, instead of relying on the speech alone.

qa.q: How does Vijay see the councillor?
qa.a: Vijay sees her as possibly good in some ways and questionable in others, someone to judge by her record.

grounding: It shows a teen thrilled by a charismatic leader's speech who enjoys the inspiration, then asks what she actually does, who benefits and what is hidden.
